extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians, comedy writers, and critics interested in Norm MacDonald–style humor
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for constructing jokes in the Norm MacDonald vein: setup-heavy, earnest, quasi-anti-comedy that often subverts form by lengthening setup and delivering a corny or offhand punch. Emphasizes surprise, form-awareness, and delivery without 'winking.'

rubrics_metrics.name: A joke should catch someone by surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: "A joke should catch someone by surprise." (Mission statement.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies not just to a punchline but to the whole meandering, straightlaced, sometimes anti-humorous path the joke takes — the shock can come from the form or the delivery, not only the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup-Heavy Construction
rubrics_metrics.description: The setup matters more than the punchline; long, winding setups that test audience patience; meandering paths to the punch; sometimes the 'point' is that there isn't one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor extended, patient setups that build expectation (or boredom). The distance traveled by the setup is itself a tool — the audience's impatience or investment becomes material for the laugh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the setup take significantly longer than expected?
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubric item: Does the setup take significantly longer than expected?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for setups that deliberately exceed normal pacing; examples include multi-minute narratives that appear aimless. The longer-than-expected setup creates a tension that makes the punchline (or its corny quality) meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the punchline disproportionately corny?
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubric item: Is the punchline disproportionately corny?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The joke often hinges on a mismatch: a very long, sophisticated setup resolves in a simple, corny, or even children's-joke punch. That discrepancy is the comedic payoff — the 'fail' functions as the win.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earnest delivery (no winking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubric item / trademark: Is the delivery earnest, with no winking at the audience?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver lines straight-faced and without signaling irony. Earnestness disarms cynicism and lets the audience respond to form-level subversion rather than to an overt performance of cleverness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sudden punctuation / offhand punch
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark technique: the punch is offhand, not telegraphed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid telegraphing the payoff; the punch should arrive as a casual, almost incidental note after a long setup, increasing its comic effect by contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wink-less irony
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark technique: ironic without seeming ironic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The act is ironic in effect but presented sincerely; do not signal the irony to the audience. This maintains ambiguity about whether the comic 'knows' they're being ironic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Old-Fashioned premise
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark technique: jokes that sound like 1950s formats (an 'old-fashioned premise').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use premises or conventions that read as outdated or retro; exaggerating an old joke format can make contemporary audiences react to the form itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasi-Anti-Comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Not strictly anti-comedy — no revealing of artifice — but a 'hyper-exaggerated version of outdated joke format' that pushes the joke toward its own collapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for something adjacent to anti-comedy: subvert expectations of structure and payoff without breaking the illusion of 'serious' performance. Let the joke verge on failure so the failure becomes the comic achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the joke comment on the joke form itself?
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubric item: Does the joke comment on the joke form itself?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer jokes that operate metatextually, making the audience aware of joke mechanics (setup/punchline expectations) so the laughter can be about form as much as content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the audience laugh at form, not just content?
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubric item: Does the audience laugh at the form and structure (the subversion) rather than only at the topical content?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether laughs come from recognition of the subversion — e.g., the long setup + corny punch — versus simple content-based humor. Norm-style laughs often reward an appreciation of form.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Moth Joke (exemplar of the form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: iconic 'moth' joke — a 6+ minute setup involving a moth at a podiatrist's office whose punchline is essentially a children's joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as archetype: the comedy arises from the discrepancy between the extended, earnest setup and the mundane/corny punchline. The audience laughs at the subversion of narrative and form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why it works: destabilization, multi-level functioning, and earnestness
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanatory criterion: Audience trained on modern comedy is destabilized; the joke functions on multiple levels — corny on the surface, sophisticated about form; earnestness disarms cynicism; the 'fail' is the win.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a joke accomplishes these effects: it should unsettle modern comedic expectations, operate simultaneously as a simple joke and a commentary on joke-making, and use straight delivery to turn apparent failure into success.
